title: Dark Web Monitoring
summary: Dark web monitoring is the systematic collection and analysis of content from sources that mainstream search engines do not index, including criminal forums, illicit marketplaces, paste sites, private messaging channels, ransomware leak sites and credential dumps, in order to detect exposure, fraud enablers and threats to an organisation. For defenders it supports four main use cases: discovering leaked or stolen credentials and session material before it is used, identifying brand impersonation and phishing infrastructure, learning about planned or ongoing campaigns that name the organisation or its suppliers, and gathering adversary tradecraft that can be turned into detection. Collection is harder than it first appears. Sources are ephemeral and hostile, registration often requires vouching or payment, access carries legal, contractual and personal safety risk, and much of the content is recycled, fabricated or seeded by criminals and by researchers themselves. Verification is therefore the core analyst skill: a credential listing proves nothing until a controlled check confirms it is current, and a forum post claiming an intrusion may simply be a sales pitch. Sound programmes use dedicated isolated collection environments, maintain strict separation between collection identities and corporate infrastructure, operate under rules of engagement approved by legal and leadership, and handle material that may contain personal data in line with privacy regulation. Output is only valuable when it reaches a workflow, so mature teams route validated findings into identity remediation, takedown requests, fraud monitoring and intelligence reporting, and they record which sources produced results and which produced noise.
objectives: You will be able to define collection requirements that connect dark web monitoring to specific defensive decisions.
You will be able to explain the legal, privacy and personal safety constraints that govern covert collection and reporting.
You will be able to validate leaked credential and access listings before triggering remediation or escalation.
You will be able to distinguish genuine exposure from recycled, fabricated or researcher-seeded content.
You will be able to route validated findings into identity, fraud, takedown and intelligence workflows.
You will be able to measure source productivity and retire collection that generates noise without decisions.
